problem:
The population of a bacterial culture $P(t)$ after $t$ hours can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=-P.
$$

If there are currently $30$ bacteria in the culture, calculate the population after $3$ hours. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

The population after $3$ hours is approximately 
{{field-1}}
bacteria.
worked_solution:
We model the population using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=-P.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)={P}_{0}\,{e}^{-t},
$$

where ${P}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that there are currently $30$ bacteria in the culture, so we have ${P}_{0}=30.$

Therefore, the population $P$ at time $t$ is

$$
P(t)=30\,{e}^{-t}.
$$

Finally, to find the population when $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3) & =30\,{e}^{-1\cdot 3} \\  & =30\,{e}^{-3} \\  & ≈1.49\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that the population after $3$ hours is approximately $1$ bacterium.
